needs: Record daily habits quickly on phone and desktop with repeated timed events.
Associate a tracking day and its after-midnight events with the appropriate following main night.
Export collected data for later comparison with Garmin outside the MVP.
context: Round 1 user answers are preserved in docs/mvp-answers-round-1.md and normalized in docs/mvp-questions.md; F1-F7 are the remaining follow-ups.
Confirmed: online-only quick capture, separate repeated intakes with reusable favorites, 04:00 tracking-day boundary with manual reassignment and Europe/Paris initially.

Confirmed: green tea, black tea, mate and infusions with volume; repeatable activity type/start/duration; dinner time only; naps start/duration; non-caffeinated evening drink context separate from caffeinated intakes.

Confirmed: stress absent/medium/high with experienced and anticipated stress kept distinct; early waking is a planned constraint; unrestricted past corrections; fixed factors; no reminders or manual sleep measurements.

Pending F1-F7: registration/login policy, custom drink categories and units, exercise options, alcohol/gluten granularity, late-sugar rule, drink/cat detail, exact stress periods, early-wake fields, note meaning, export formats and unusual night defaults.
The user delegates stack selection: retain React/TypeScript, FastAPI, SQLite and Docker. Domain/proxy integration remains a later hosting decision.
Public source repository; personal data and Garmin exports remain private. Garmin integration, correlations and production deployment are outside current work.
acceptance_criteria: AC1: Deliver an authenticated French mobile-first installable PWA with online-only quick event buttons and server-persisted records shared across phone and desktop sessions; disconnected or failed saves never appear successful and no offline write queue is implemented.

AC2: Preserve actual timestamps and offsets alongside a tracking-day date and stable editable main-night association; apply a 04:00 local boundary in Europe/Paris, test midnight/boundary/DST/manual reassignment, and create nominal night IDs without requiring actual sleep metrics.

AC3: Support separate repeated timed beverage intakes with distinct green tea, black tea, mate and infusion categories, volume and reusable favorites; keep non-caffeinated evening hot-drink context distinct, resolve F2/F4 detail and avoid duplicate intake records.

AC4: Support repeatable physical activities with type, start and duration and naps with start plus duration; validate duration consistency, and resolve F2 before adding intensity or multi-activity sessions.

AC5: Capture dinner time only with independent alcohol/gluten answers and late sugar; preserve unknown versus explicit absence, and resolve F3 granularity and the fixed late threshold before implementing dependent validation.

AC6: Capture night cat presence, experienced and anticipated stress as separate absent/medium/high values, and a planned early-wake constraint; resolve F4/F5 period/time/reason detail and never substitute actual stress for an earlier anticipation.

AC7: Provide history with unrestricted past creation/correction and deletion, preserve repeated entries and explicit negative versus missing answers without a mandatory recap; keep the factor list fixed and resolve F6 before adding the requested note control near actions.

AC8: Export all history with complete collected entities and relationships, IDs, timezone/offset, original timestamps, units, missingness, tracking days, night links and distinct stress semantics; confirm versioned JSON and normalized CSV bundle in F7 and verify completeness using synthetic round-trip fixtures.

AC9: Keep Garmin imports/synchronization/credentials, correlations, health recommendations, manual sleep measurements and reminders outside the MVP; document future external Garmin joins using nominal night labels without inventing actual bedtime/wake time or Garmin values.

AC10: Provide reproducible local startup, a container deployment artifact, persistent storage and documented backup/restore; verify authentication and isolation of private data, and commit synthetic data only; do not deploy production as part of planning.

product.title: SommeilEnOr personal sleep context journal
product.overview: A fast French PWA to collect daily and nightly context and export it for later sleep analysis.
goals: Fast online-only quick-action capture with reusable favorites and unrestricted historical correction.
Reliable temporal links across midnight and devices.
Complete portable records with explicit missingness.
non_goals: Correlation dashboards, causal claims or health recommendations.
Production deployment during initial corpus creation.
Offline writes or synchronization, reminders, manual sleep metrics, mixed-drink composition and a generic custom-factor builder.

backlog_items.title: Define tracking days nights and collection data contracts
problem: Midnight and ambiguous missing values can make future sleep comparisons incorrect.
scope_in: Use the confirmed 04:00 Europe/Paris tracking-day boundary and manual main-night reassignment; resolve F7 unusual nocturnal events.
Define tracking days, nominal nights, intake/session records, favorites, assessments, stable IDs, units and missingness; no manual sleep metrics are required.
Resolve F3/F5 granularity and assessed periods before finalizing related contracts; keep anticipated and experienced stress distinct.
Priority rationale: temporal identity and missingness are dependencies of every capture screen.
scope_out: Garmin integration, correlations and production deployment.
acceptance_criteria: AC1: Document 00:30, 03:59, 04:00 and 08:00 mapping, DST/offset preservation and manual override without requiring bedtime or actual wake time.
AC2: Define experienced/anticipated stress as distinct absent/medium/high fields with explicit assessed periods resolved in F5.
AC3: Define unknown/none/not-applicable semantics, reusable favorite identity and migration-safe full-history export contracts.

backlog_items.title: Build authenticated cross-device PWA foundation
problem: A public repository must deliver a private journal usable across devices.
scope_in: Confirm registration/login policy in F1; online-only behavior and chosen React/TypeScript + FastAPI + SQLite stack are settled.
French responsive quick-action shell, install manifest and service worker/update behavior without journal write caching.
Authenticated API, server persistence, sessions, mutation protection and account data isolation if registration is enabled.
Visible pending/saved/failed/disconnected states; no offline queue or automatic replay.
Priority rationale: access control and reliable persistence precede personal-data collection.
scope_out: Garmin integration, correlations and production deployment.
acceptance_criteria: AC1: Verify unauthenticated users cannot read, mutate or export journal data.
AC2: Demonstrate a saved record is visible on a second authenticated browser and layouts work on mobile and desktop.
AC3: Verify HTTPS installability and updates; offline/failed writes show a truthful state, create no queued journal entry and are not silently replayed.

backlog_items.title: Collect repeated beverages physical activities and naps
problem: Repeated daily events cannot be represented by one boolean per category.
scope_in: Green tea, black tea, mate and infusions with time and volume; separate repeated intakes and reusable favorites. Resolve custom categories/units in F2.
Quick create and historical editing; favorites create fresh independently editable entries. Mixed-ingredient composition is outside requested scope.
Repeatable physical activity type/start/duration and naps start/duration; resolve initial activities and optional intensity/compound sessions in F2.
Keep non-caffeinated evening context separate and resolve F4 detail without duplicating infusion events.
Priority rationale: timed repeated events are the core collection workflow.
scope_out: Garmin integration, correlations and production deployment.
acceptance_criteria: AC1: Save multiple green teas, black tea, mate and infusion records with time and volume; reuse a favorite without overwriting previous entries.
AC2: Create/edit repeated activity sessions and naps using start plus duration; reject invalid durations and preserve manual night overrides.
AC3: Keep the non-caffeinated evening context distinct from caffeinated intakes and avoid double counting one infusion as two drinks.

backlog_items.title: Collect meal night context and daily assessments
problem: Meal and night context needs clear granularity and meaningful unanswered states.
scope_in: Dinner time only, independently editable alcohol/gluten and late sugar; resolve F3 granularity and threshold.
Night cat presence and distinct experienced/anticipated absent/medium/high stress; resolve F4/F5 exact detail.
Planned early-wake constraint only; resolve target time and reason in F5.
Fixed initial factors; resolve F6 note-control meaning before implementing that control.
Priority rationale: complete the requested factor set after shared capture patterns exist.
scope_out: Garmin integration, correlations and production deployment.
Manual sleep metrics, actual early-wake measurements, reminders and generic custom factors.
acceptance_criteria: AC1: Save dinner time independently of alcohol/gluten/sugar, cat presence and planned early-wake context; distinguish unanswered from explicit absence.
AC2: Preserve separate experienced and anticipated stress at absent/medium/high with explicit assessed periods; editing actual stress does not overwrite anticipation.
AC3: Export the agreed planned early-wake and late-sugar meaning; after F6 is answered, verify the requested note control and its data semantics.

backlog_items.title: Deliver day night history and portable exports
problem: The collection MVP must already produce reliable inputs for later external comparisons.
scope_in: Day/night navigation with unrestricted historical creation, editing, deletion and missingness; no mandatory daily recap.
All-history export; confirm versioned JSON and normalized CSV bundle in F7 and document the data dictionary.
Include repeated events, favorites, any confirmed notes, distinct stress assessments and editable nominal-night associations.
Document future Garmin matching by nominal night date and stored offsets, without measured wake dates or integration.
Priority rationale: useful history and lossless export complete the collection promise.
scope_out: Garmin integration, correlations and production deployment.
acceptance_criteria: AC1: Export a synthetic journal spanning midnight and DST, repeated events and missing/negative answers; compare every exported entity and relationship to persisted data.
AC2: Demonstrate historical time edits and night overrides remain consistent in history and export.
AC3: Ensure exports are authenticated, omit secrets, and contain no fabricated Garmin or correlation fields.

backlog_items.title: Package and verify collection MVP for self hosting
problem: A cross-device journal needs reproducible operations and recoverable persistent storage.
scope_in: Use the retained React/TypeScript + FastAPI + SQLite/Docker stack; implement no offline synchronization or reminders.
Document local startup and selected dependency versions, container build and generic HTTPS reverse-proxy integration.
Use environment templates without real deployment addresses or credentials.
Document and exercise backup/restore with synthetic data and persistent volumes.
Focused integration and responsive-browser checks; French i18n contract validation.
Priority rationale: operational verification is required before any later deployment.
scope_out: Garmin integration, correlations and production deployment.
acceptance_criteria: AC1: Start a clean instance from documented commands and verify a restart preserves synthetic journal entries.
AC2: Restore a synthetic backup into an isolated instance and compare records and exported links.
AC3: Run the relevant automated checks and mobile/desktop smoke checks; record evidence without claiming production deployment.
